 This application coming on for admission this day, the   following:
 ORDER

Petitioners have filed this petition under Section 482 of Code of Criminal Procedure to quash Complaint Case No. 664/2017 and also to quash consequential proceedings arising out of said complaint, which is pending before Judicial Magistrate First Class, Mauganj, District Rewa (M.P.).
2.

Counsel appearing for petitioners submitted that respondent No. 2 has filed a complaint, in which allegations were made that petitioners, who are respondents No. 1 to 4, acting in collusion with revenue officers got a trace map prepared, by which land belonging to complainant-respondent No.2 was shown in land belonging to petitioners.
Counsel appearing for petitioners submitted that no offence under Sections 420, 424 or 471 of Indian Penal Code is made out against petitioners.
It is submitted that there was no misrepresentation and inducement by present petitioners on basis of which respondent No. 2 had delivered any property to them.
It is submitted that in revenue proceedings, trace map was prepared and therefore, said act cannot be said to be an offence.
It is further submitted that offence under Sections 424 and 471 are also not made out as no forgery has been done by petitioners and they had not prepared any forged documents.
Documents were prepared in revenue proceedings in accordance with law.
In these circumstances, complaint case against petitioners be quashed.
3. None appeared for respondent No. 2 though, notices has been served.

In these circumstances,
respondent No. 2 is proceeded exparte.
4. Government Advocate appearing for respondent No.1/State supported the order passed by the trial Court dated 03.03.2017.

It is submitted that trial Court has taken into consideration complaint and statements of Daddi Baksh and Govind Prasad Shrivastava and thereafter, cognizance of offences under Sections 120-B, 218, 420, 424 and 471 of IPC was taken by trial Court.
No error can be found in the order.
Petitioners have cheated respondent No.2 by taking away his valuable land.
In these circumstances, no interference is called for and petition be dismissed.

5. Heard the counsel for the parties.
6. Sections 420, 424 and 471 of IPC are reproduced as under :

Dishonest or fraudulent removal or concealment of property.--Whoever dishonestly or fraudulently conceals or removes any property of himself or any other person, or dishonestly or fraudulently assists in the concealment or removal thereof,
or dishonestly releases any demand or claim to which he is entitled, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.
471. Using as genuine a forged [document or electronic record].--Whoever fraudulently or dishonestly uses as genuine any [document or electronic record]
which he knows or has reason to believe to be a forged [document or electronic record], shall be punished in the same manner as if he had forged such [document or electronic record]."
7. On going through aforesaid sections, it is clear that to make out an offence, there has to be an inducement and cheating and on basis of said inducement and cheating, victim have transferred valuable property or security in favour of accused persons.
In the present case, there was no misrepresentation or cheating.
Trace map was prepared by revenue officers and there was no inducement and neither there was any delivery of property by respondent No. 2 to petitioners.
In these circumstances, offence under Section 420 of IPC is not made out.
8. On going through facts of the case, it is also found that there is no fraudulent removal or concealment of property to deprive respondent No.2 of his property.
Offence under Section 471 of IPC is also not made out as petitioners could not be said to have used any forged document as genuine.
Document in question has been prepared under M.P. Land Revenue Code and Rules made therein.
Trace map may be wrong or incorrect, but, that will not make a document to be a forged document.
9. Considering aforesaid circumstances, petition filed by petitioners is allowed.
